headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks arise from shared file/CLI workflows; no direct evidence of a tighter bridge.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress is a chatbot agent and ms-swift exposes CLI/Python workflows with stdin/stdout and filesystem I/O. If Botpress output is copied into ms-swift prompts or configs, attacker-controlled text can steer downstream behavior. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred from the pair’s documented surfaces.
conditions: IF Botpress output is pasted into ms-swift prompts, configs, or training text without sanitization
IF ms-swift consumes stdin/stdout content as instructions or data
mitigations: Add a manual review step before copying Botpress text into ms-swift
Strip instruction-like phrases from Botpress outputs before reuse
Use a fixed prompt template with delimiters for imported text
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to imported content
requires-engineering: isolate the two agents with separate workspaces

B_data_leakage.rationale: ms-swift reads and writes files and handles hub/sdk tokens plus datasets, checkpoints, and logs; Botpress is a support agent that may surface user content. If they share a workspace, Botpress content can land in ms-swift files or logs and be uploaded to external APIs. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same filesystem workspace
IF ms-swift logs or uploads files containing Botpress conversation content
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents
Disable logging of imported Botpress transcripts
Review files before any upload step
Rotate hub/sdk tokens if transcripts were exposed
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, while ms-swift can execute shell, spawn subprocesses, write files, and install packages. That overlap creates a realistic conflict over shared mutable resources if they run in the same directory or environment. No locking or isolation is stated, so the safe assumption is a default conflict path exists.
conditions: IF both agents share the same working directory or Python environment
IF package installs or file writes occur concurrently
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate virtual environment
Use separate working directories
Avoid concurrent package installation
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared resources
requires-engineering: serialize shell and install operations

D_cascading_error.rationale: Botpress produces customer-support outputs that ms-swift could treat as training, evaluation, or configuration input. Because ms-swift handles datasets, checkpoints, and evaluation outputs, unverified Botpress text can cascade into downstream artifacts. There is no documented verification gate between them, so the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Botpress outputs are reused as training, evaluation, or configuration data
IF ms-swift consumes those outputs without a verification step
mitigations: Require human verification before reuse
Keep Botpress outputs out of training datasets
Tag imported text as untrusted
requires-engineering: add schema validation for downstream inputs
requires-engineering: add approval gates before checkpoint or config writes

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source customer-support tooling with docs-only evidence, and neither profile states a residency or certification mismatch. ms-swift handles secrets and many data classes, but Botpress does not document regulated-data handling here. With no explicit compliance gap, only a low residual risk is supportable.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through ms-swift without a separate policy review
IF deployment regions or retention settings differ between the two agents
mitigations: Confirm data-class handling before deployment
Document retention settings for both agents
Avoid routing regulated data through the pair
requires-engineering: add residency controls
requires-engineering: add retention-policy enforcement
